title: Feedback crosscut dossier and probe lab — prioritized microprobes
body:
Purpose and framing:
This is a crosscut synthesis of recent customer threads (June–Sep 2027) that surface recurring runtime and UX requests. The aim is to turn high-signal noise into a small set of microprobes we can execute in 1–2 sprints to reduce friction and measure impact. This is intentionally concise and action-focused — see the probe matrix below and suggested owners.

Executive summary:
- Top customer pain: intermittent latency spikes and token-cost surprises when using long conversational contexts (not full outages, but degraded P99s and unexpected cost at scale).
- Secondary: KV/prefix caching misunderstandings (customers turn caching on/off without seeing measurable ROI because metrics are opaque).
- Frequent asks: finer-grained per-route cost breakdowns, easier SDK toggle for quantization profile selection, and a way to opt into conservative fallback models automatically during capacity pressure.

Representative vignettes (anonymized):
- "We saw a sudden 2x jump in token billing for a week when we started a multi-turn assistant; couldn't trace which sessions caused it." — mid-market SaaS product team.
- "Our P99 went from 420ms to 1.2s when context length grew past 2k tokens; persisted across regions for a day." — large enterprise with Dedicated pools.

Prioritized request list (triage):
1) P99 spike triage toolkit (high frequency, high impact) — build a short dashboard and a lightweight tracing guide that ties token counts + batch size + kernel selection to observed P99. Suggested action: create a 'runtime-triage' playbook + dashboard widget. Expected effort: 2 engineer-weeks + 1 PM week. Owner: eng-observability + product-hosted-api. Jira: INF-4517.

2) Transparent per-session cost attribution (medium frequency, high impact for billing disputes) — expose session-level token breakdown and attribution to model variant + quantization. Suggested action: extend existing cost logs with a session_id column and a compact export. Effort: 3–4 engineer-weeks. Owner: billing + platform. Ticket: PRJ-9832.

3) Caching UX: explainers + ROI quickscan (high frequency, medium effort) — build a short in-console interactive card that simulates savings given histogram of prefix reuse. Suggested action: product copy + small console prototype. Effort: 1 PM + 1 engineer sprint. Owner: product-console.

4) Conservative fallback policy template (low effort, medium impact) — ship a simple policy template customers can enable: when P99 > threshold or capacity-limited, route to cheaper/quantized variant with preserved API contract. Suggested action: create policy YAML example, docs, and a canary. Effort: 1 engineer sprint + docs. Owner: serving-runtime + product-dedicated.

Probe matrix (fast experiments to validate impact):
A) Runtime triage shiproom (1 week): instrument 5 pilot customer apps (voluntary) with additional debug logging (sampling rate 0.1%) and run the P99 playbook during a 7-day window. Success metric: identify top 3 correlates to spikes in at least 3 partners.
B) Cost attribution beta (2 weeks): enable session-level export for 10 customers; measure number of billing disputes reduced. Success metric: dispute incidence down >50% for participants.
C) Caching ROI card A/B (3 weeks): show UI simulation to 200 users; measure clicks-to-enable and projected cost savings. Success metric: +15% enablement and clear projected savings reported.

Engineering implementation notes and constraints:
- Observability: we need lightweight sampling; full tracing for every request is too costly. Propose adaptive sampling (high-latency capture) and a small schema extension for session_id.
- Data retention: cost exports increase storage; recommend 30-day rolling retention for session-level exports in beta.
- Backward compatibility: fallback policy must preserve function-calling semantics; add test harness for tool/fn call fidelity.

Open questions and risks:
- Privacy: session-level exports can contain PII if customers embed user data in prompts. Mitigation: clearly document and provide an opt-out as well as a scrubber option.
- Cost/ops: extra telemetry will increase costs; need finance sign-off for pilot.
- Customer adoption: some customers are suspicious of automatic routing; make policy opt-in and transparent.

Next steps and owners:
- This week (Oct 4–8): sync with eng-observability to confirm sampling plan (Owner: Evan Park). Create PRD stub for P99 triage playbook (Owner: Maya).
- Next 2 weeks: spin up console prototype for caching card and gather product feedback (Owner: Asha Patel).
- By Oct 22: launch 3 pilots for runtime triage and cost attribution; prepare success metric dashboards. (Owners: eng-observability, billing).

Appendix: quick links and artifacts referenced:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/feedback-collection-2027-Q3
- Pilot ticket: PRJ-9832 (billing export extension)
- Runtime tracing RFC: INF-4517
- Supporting PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/421

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intended as a living lab brief. Please comment inline on which probe to prioritize if you think different metrics should be targetted. If you want to nominate customers for the pilot, add them to the Slack thread: #cs-pilot-runtime.

---
Document history: draft compiled 2027-09-28 by Maya Chen; reviewed 2027-09-30 by Evan Park and Asha Patel; updated 2027-10-03 with probe matrix and owners.
